claim: A rename carries a page's `.uncommitted.ts` sidecar to the new path and leaves the export name inside it spelled from the old slug. The sidecar is generated, and the name it exports is composed from the page's own path, so a rename that does not respell it leaves the file saying it belongs to a page that is no longer there. Nothing reads that name and the next write recomposes it, so the staleness costs nothing until an agent has to spell it by hand, once for every page renamed.

evidence:
`infrastructure/service/workstation/pages/temper-addon-deploying/temper-addon-deploying.service-workstation.uncommitted.ts` reads `export const esoAddonDeployingServiceWorkstationUncommitted = {` after the page was renamed from `eso-addon-deploying` to `temper-addon-deploying`. The file moved; the name inside it did not. Reproduced by drafting `rename-page` over `alan/harness/errors-core/runtime-error/pages/alanwalton-0469101fb6a3ea5c.runtime-error.ts` to `alanwalton-0469101fb6a3ea5d`: the sidecar landed at the new path still reading `export const alanwalton0469101fb6a3ea5cRuntimeErrorUncommitted = {`.

The name is composed by `nameFor` in `page/modules/uncommitted/page-uncommitted.module.code.ts`, which spells `exportedAs([said.slug, said.pageType, ...said.sections, HOLDS].join("-"))` off the page's path, and `bodyFor` beside it writes `export const ${nameFor(page)} = ...`. `pageRenamed` in `change/modules/page-renaming/page-renaming.module.code.ts` gathers the sidecar through `reservedIn` and `uncommittedAt` and hands it to `carriedBy` in `change/modules/file-carrying/file-carrying.module.code.ts`, which answered the moves and the repointing and nothing else, so the body travelled unread. `spellingsIn` in `page/modules/export-name/modules/export-spelling/export-spelling.module.code.ts` respells the page's own `export type` and the `.code.ts` sibling's `export const`, and reaches no sidecar.

What it cost: renaming twenty add-on pages from `temper-<x>-addon` to `temper-addon-<x>` took twenty separate `change-file` calls, one for each page's `.uncommitted.ts` sibling. Twenty hand steps that should have been none, and the recipe agents were handed said to make them.

What makes it easy to miss: nothing reads that name. `loadedFrom` in `page/modules/value/page-value.module.code.ts` takes `firstValueIn(declaredIn(body))` and ignores the identifier, so a stale name loads exactly as a current one does, and the next call to `mergeUncommitted` or `changeUncommitted` recomposes the whole body through `bodyFor`. The staleness heals itself on the next write, so it never breaks anything and is never noticed. It lasts only where nothing writes the file for days, which is what a deploy sidecar is. Measured over the checkout: 478 `.uncommitted.ts` files and exactly one stale; and of the only other generated family whose body carries a slug-derived name, 2,375 `.types.ts` files, none stale, because a refresh regenerates every one of them.

Mended in `8748eed9d7172dd0580c4624d04afb9a38f423b1`, which has `carriedBy` write such a sidecar again through `bodyFor`.

The condition a mend would meet: a change that lands a page's `.uncommitted.ts` beside a page of another name writes that sidecar's body again through the writer that composes it, so the name it exports is the name that writer would compose there.
